about: Every utterance in Pet Island that needs synthesizing. Per docs/pet-island-voice.md §5.1.
This is a RUNNING file: no spoken line may be added to the island without an entry here.
Text is the TARGET wording — i.e. after the splice law of voice.md §3. Where the shipped
code still differs, the entry carries "port": the item that brings the code into line.
The 2D game (src/words2d, v0/junos-words.html) is NOT covered here. It is frozen and its
speech must stay identical to v0, including the spoken child's name at v0:742. The splice

voices.fred: Warm, playful, slower. The island's host. Never speaks a dynamic name.
voices.teacher: One clear British voice, never varies. Owns every challenge word and every pet name — consistency is part of the listening task.
voices.owl: Measured, warm. Not used this phase.
voices.dad: Parent recordings from the sound booth. Phoneme clips and school-list imports.

laws: No character speaks a dynamic name mid-sentence. The child's name is print only; spoken address is 'friend'.
A slotted template and its inserts share one voice. Cross-voice splices are forbidden.
A pet's name is always the teacher's, never a character's — so a name is a line of its own, chained between character lines rather than spliced into one.

generated.source: build-time name table, one entry per {setId, speciesId}
generated.note: Fixed per variant and identical on every island (brief §5, voice.md §2). Graded by set: set 1 at band 1, climbing. Audited before bake; a rejected name is replaced at authoring time, never dropped.
Repeat-on-tap plays the same clip at rate 0.6; grapheme-by-grapheme help plays at 0.9 (src/challenges/build.ts:83,96).

lines.text: I'm Fred. It's just me on this little rock.
It's ever so quiet out here.
Eggs come from far across the sea… and they only hatch for someone who reads to them.
Will you read to it, friend?

lines.note: Beat 7 is now three chained lines, not one. Fred, then the teacher announcing the name, then Fred again — a name is never in a character's mouth.
Plays the pet's clip from the name table.

lines.text: Home at last! It was coming home all along.
lines.was: You found its name! [PETNAME] has arrived.

lines.text: Every friend you read home needs somewhere to live… can you count us up some land?
